topic: Panel bucking, estimation of compressive loads for bucking a panel on simply supported structures
syllabus_extract: Panel bucking, estimation of compressive loads for bucking a panel on simply supported structures. Rigidity due to end conditions on panel, study of heads, to bend panel with regards to variation in end condition shear buckling of plates
specific_objectives: 11.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain aircraft structure, various structural elements and their details.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of panel buckling under compressive load; Safety: Ensure load application is controlled; Supervision: Instructor monitors load limits and panel integrity
intro_questions: What is the primary failure mode for thin skin panels under compression?
Define simply supported boundary conditions for a structural panel.
How does end rigidity affect the critical buckling load of a panel?

development.content:
Definition of panel bucking
Estimation of compressive loads
Simply supported structures analysis
Critical load calculation methods

summary_questions: Explain how end condition rigidity alters the critical buckling load.
Describe the relationship between shear buckling and plate geometry.
Identify two factors that increase the compressive load capacity of a panel.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the repair scheme considerations for a panel damaged due to buckling, referencing the next lesson plan (LP 17).

pft_rows.syllabus: Assessment of damage and estimation of loads, preparation of repair scheme. Material specification, special tools required for carrying out repairs
